info.name: Citizens
info.summary: Run in-person citizens' assemblies: offline-first table recording, transcription and evidence-linked analysis
info.description:
Citizens supports **in-person citizens' assemblies and deliberative workshops**. One ordinary phone per discussion table records the conversation, and the app turns those recordings into transcripts, per-table summaries and cross-table findings that a human organizer reviews before anything is published.
## How it works
1. Create an assembly with its rounds and questions, and print one QR code per table. 2. Each table opens its code on a phone. Recording is **offline-first**: audio is stored on the device first and uploaded when the network allows, so a bad connection can never lose a discussion. 3. Run the assembly in **live mode** (you start and end each round for every table at once) or **independent mode** (each table records the shared questions on its own schedule, even days apart). 4. Recordings are transcribed (with speaker diarization on engines that support it) and analyzed per table, then aggregated across tables into points of consensus, points of divergence, proposals, concerns and open questions — every finding linked to the exact passage that supports it. 5. You review and approve findings, close the session, and export the final report as PDF, Markdown or JSON. Reports can be published back to the table phones so participants see the outcome of their own discussion.
The phone recorder — including the information screen people read before being recorded — is shown in the language of the assembly rather than of the phone, since it is a device shared by the whole table. English and Italian are available today.
## Data processing — please read
This app records people's voices, which is sensitive personal data.
* **Nothing is sent anywhere until an administrator configures a key.** A fresh install performs no transcription and no analysis. * **Speech-to-text** (both the live captions shown while recording and the final transcript): four engines are supported. Deepgram and Mistral are hosted services — with those, the assembled audio of a recording is sent to the provider once for transcription, and, if live captions are on, in ~10-second pieces while the table is speaking. **Whisper** works against any OpenAI-compatible endpoint, including one you run yourself, and **Vosk** runs entirely offline on your own server; with either of those, audio never leaves your infrastructure. * Transcription of the finished audio can be switched off, in which case the live captions become the assembly's transcript and nothing is sent a second time. Reports built that way say so, because captions can miss speech an engine could not keep up with. * **Analysis**: when an administrator configures an analysis endpoint, only the *transcript text* (never audio) is sent to it. Any OpenAI-compatible endpoint works, so this step can run entirely on your own infrastructure — for example a self-hosted Ollama or vLLM server. * **Everything else stays on your server**: audio files, transcripts, findings and reports live in the app's own storage, never in users' Nextcloud files. * Organizers can download or **delete audio and transcripts** at any time from the Files tab of each assembly, without deleting the assembly itself.
Full note: https://github.com/Democracy-Routes/nextcloud-citizens/blob/main/docs/privacy.md
## Ethical AI Rating
**Rating: 🟢 Green when self-hosted, 🟠 orange with hosted providers.** Both transcription and analysis can run entirely on your own infrastructure: Whisper through any OpenAI-compatible server (Speaches, whisper.cpp, LocalAI, vLLM, WhisperX) or Vosk fully offline, with analysis against a local Ollama or vLLM endpoint. Nothing leaves your servers in that configuration, the software is AGPL, and transcription stays off until you configure an engine. Choosing the hosted options (Deepgram, Mistral, OpenAI) sends audio or transcripts to a third party whose models are not freely available — that is the orange case. See https://nextcloud.com/blog/nextcloud-ethical-ai-rating/
## Status
This is a **beta release**. The recording, transcription, analysis and reporting pipeline is tested end to end. Audio retention is configurable (delete N days after an assembly is closed, with a per-assembly override), and the recorder shows each table an information screen before recording starts, naming the transcription engine, whether it is an outside service, and how long audio is kept. That screen offers a decline as well as a confirmation.
That screen is an information and confirmation step at the table, **not** a per-individual consent record — Citizens does not store who agreed. Organisations whose lawful basis requires individual consent should collect it separately, and should run a rehearsal before a high-stakes assembly.
